claims.text: Replacing tungsten and tantalum with titanium and chromium while retaining vanadium will reduce neutron activation.
The modified refractory HEA will maintain the high-temperature mechanical strength needed for plasma-facing components.
The modified refractory HEA will maintain irradiation resistance.
W-Ta-Cr-V is a refractory high-entropy alloy system.
The W-Ta-Cr-V HEA has high mechanical strength and resistance to irradiation-induced loops and helium-bubble formation.
The W-Ta-Cr-V HEA demonstrates excellent high-temperature performance.
The tungsten-based initial HEA suffers from potentially high neutron activation.
Tungsten and tantalum are high-activation refractory elements, whereas titanium and chromium are low-activation refractory elements.
Retaining vanadium will preserve high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance after the substitution.
Fusion plasma-facing materials must operate at temperatures of at least 1000 K while exposed to D/T species, helium, and neutrons.
The modified alloy will form and retain a single-phase BCC microstructure typical of refractory HEAs.
A single-phase BCC microstructure is key to high-temperature stability and irradiation resistance.
Substitution of high-activation elements by lower-activation elements reduces production of long-lived radioactive isotopes under neutron irradiation.
The refractory HEA microstructure intrinsically provides mechanical robustness and irradiation tolerance.
The modified alloy will have significantly lower post-irradiation radioactivity than the tungsten-based HEA.
The modified alloy will have high-temperature mechanical properties comparable to those of the tungsten-based counterpart.
The modified alloy will resist irradiation-induced damage comparably to the tungsten-based counterpart.
Tungsten-based HEAs or tungsten alloys perform well mechanically at high temperature.
Tungsten-based HEAs or tungsten alloys are limited by production of high long-term radioactivity under neutron irradiation.
Performance under fusion conditions may not translate to lower-temperature or less irradiative environments.
